title: Itchan Kala, the walled inner town of Khiva
summary: Itchan Kala is the walled inner town of Khiva, Uzbekistan, a rectangle of 650 by 400 m inside brick walls about 10 m high. Ramparts rebuilt by the Kungrats rise from 10th-11th-century substructures; its monuments illustrate Central Asian Islamic architecture from the 14th to the 19th century.

uncertainty.note: ICOMOS dates the rampart substructures to the 10th and 11th centuries (901-1100); the visible fabric is mostly 19th-century Kungrat rebuilding. End is the present.

phases.description: Begun in 1853 under Muhammad Amin Khan; work stopped in 1855 when the khan was killed (uzbekistan.travel).
Stands unfinished as a truncated cone, far shorter than intended.

reviewer_note: Modelled structure is Kalta Minor (tower, 29 m, 14.5 m diameter); the record's date range is for Itchan Kala as a whole. Kalta Minor figures vary by site (a guide site gave 26-29 m height and 14.2-14.5 m diameter) and the start year (1851, 1852, 1853); I could open only uzbekistan.travel. Material 'brick' is for the walls per UNESCO. Least sure of the 901 start. Walled town measurements (kept out of the minaret model): Itchan Kala wall height 10 m (src-unesco-543); Itchan Kala length 650 m (src-unesco-543); Itchan Kala width 400 m (src-unesco-543).
